scenes.narration_reference: Years later, the Rajasthan Royals hackathon brought that notebook back. This time, I wanted evidence. Who actually performs when the game gets difficult?

scenes.beats: Messy event cards → reject incorrect wicket attribution → sort → eligible evidence stack.
caveats: Wides/no-balls retained in bowling exposure.
Run-outs are not bowler-credited wickets.
scenes.hero_source: Retained V3/V4 head/torso sprites; no redesign
scenes.narration_reference: First obstacle: two hundred thousand delivery events. Wides. No-balls. Run-outs. Rain. Before judging a player, I had to reconstruct the match correctly.

scenes.beats: Ball about to be delivered → freeze hand → inspect state → release without showing future outcome.
caveats: Illustrative 28 from12, required rate14.
No current ball outcome in its pressure label.
scenes.hero_source: Retained V3/V4 head/torso sprites; no redesign
scenes.narration_reference: Then I froze time before every ball. Score. Wickets. Balls remaining. No peeking at the six that happened next. That would be cheating, with a spreadsheet.

scenes.beats: Impossible chase looks frightening → consequential last ball reverses interpretation → skeptical reaction.
caveats: 39 RPO and2 off1 are illustrative states, not player evidence.
scenes.hero_source: Retained V3/V4 head/torso sprites; no redesign
scenes.narration_reference: But difficult doesn't always mean consequential. Thirty-nine runs an over? Terrifying. Also, probably over. Two needed off one? Now the next ball can change everything.

scenes.beats: A pan loaded → B pan loaded → combined percentile disc → select primary pressure set.
scenes.purpose: Difficulty + WP leverage, context-relative percentile combination.
caveats: Top20% within innings, not each phase.
scenes.hero_source: Retained V3/V4 head/torso sprites; no redesign
scenes.narration_reference: So I combined scoreboard difficulty with win-probability leverage, using context-relative percentiles. The primary definition selected the top twenty percent within each innings.

scenes.beats: Celebrate raw performance → contextual expectation card arrives → compare → amend claim.
scenes.purpose: Positive residual means better than contextual expectation.
caveats: Runs/survival and runs prevented/credited wickets distinct.
Any bars are illustrative, not player estimates.
scenes.hero_source: Retained V3/V4 head/torso sprites; no redesign
scenes.narration_reference: Next question: better than what? I estimated expected runs and dismissal risk. Batters earned credit for extra runs and survival. Bowlers, for runs prevented and credited wickets.

scenes.beats: Pick15 chip → pause → compare10/20 alternatives → leave assumption visible.
scenes.purpose: 15 runs per wicket is a declared assumption.
caveats: Era/opposition adjustment
Sensitivity10 and20, no universal wicket value claim.
scenes.hero_source: Retained V3/V4 head/torso sprites; no redesign
scenes.narration_reference: I adjusted for scoring eras and opposition. Then combined runs and wickets with a declared assumption: fifteen runs per wicket. And checked ten and twenty too.

scenes.beats: Huge trophy on25-event stack → 400-event evidence arrives → suspicious glance → estimate shrinks toward mean.
scenes.purpose: Empirical Bayes corrects weakly supported estimates.
caveats: 25/400 are unnamed illustrative exposures.
No invented fitted shrinkage values.
scenes.hero_source: Retained V3/V4 head/torso sprites; no redesign
scenes.narration_reference: Then the small samples arrived, wearing enormous confidence. Twenty-five pressure events are not four hundred. Empirical Bayes pulled weakly supported estimates toward the average.

scenes.beats: Quality folder seems convincing → delta folder differs → failed bowling repeatability stamp → qualified claim.
caveats: No validated repeatable bowling delta.
Batting delta CV gains only about0.03–0.11%.
scenes.hero_source: Retained V3/V4 head/torso sprites; no redesign
scenes.narration_reference: And performing well under pressure isn't the same as improving because of pressure. Bowling showed no validated repeatable pressure delta. The batting delta gains were tiny.

scenes.beats: Confident report → sealed2026 envelope → actual weak results emerge → crestfallen → study evidence.
caveats: Batting Spearman-0.043, no positive forward signal.
Bowling+0.304 suggestive; advantage over ordinary economy not established.
First-innings WP Brier0.2559 vs0.2524 baseline, worse.
scenes.hero_source: Retained V3/V4 head/torso sprites; no redesign
scenes.narration_reference: The unseen twenty-twenty-six season challenged my story. Batting quality showed no positive predictive relationship. Bowling looked promising, but an advantage over ordinary economy wasn't established.

scenes.beats: Pick whole match cards → resample stack → uncertainty paper → caution rather than prophecy.
caveats: Conditional historical stability, not future success probability.
Illustrative distribution has no invented player CI.
scenes.hero_source: Retained V3/V4 head/torso sprites; no redesign
scenes.narration_reference: So I resampled whole matches, seven hundred and fifty times. Confidence intervals. Rank distributions. A top-ten bootstrap rate measures historical stability. It isn't a prophecy.

scenes.beats: D20 stack → D10/D25 cards → shortlist tips → best-season removal reveals fragility.
scenes.purpose: Model choices and influential seasons move the answer.
caveats: D10 retains5/10 batting,4/10 bowling.
D25 retains6/10 batting,7/10 bowling.
Removing best season drops9 names in each top10.
scenes.hero_source: Retained V3/V4 head/torso sprites; no redesign
scenes.narration_reference: Change the pressure definition, and the shortlist changes. Remove a player's best season, and nine names leave each top ten. Those weren't details to hide.

scenes.beats: Report folio opens → full batting page → full bowling page → restrained qualified reaction.
scenes.purpose: Full accepted primary top20, exposure, stability and format mix.
caveats: No new IDs/intervals.
T20I evidence not automatically IPL evidence.
scenes.hero_source: Retained V3/V4 head/torso sprites; no redesign
scenes.narration_reference: The primary lists put Jos Buttler and Jasprit Bumrah first. But every name needs its exposure, uncertainty and format mix. T-twenty international evidence isn't automatically IPL evidence.

scenes.beats: Replay papers →20/20 ranking check →41 checks → limitations remain attached.
caveats: Report-supplied claim; analytics not rerun here.
scenes.hero_source: Retained V3/V4 head/torso sprites; no redesign
scenes.narration_reference: Finally, the replay reproduced all twenty rankings and passed forty-one checks. The code repeated. The statistical limitations stayed.
